deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.22). π = π1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) is free on the loops l_0, l_1 around the three points, with l_∞ defined by l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1. Σ is the cartographic group of bicoloured maps (Malgoire–Voisin). It is an extension of Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × Z/2 by π. The index-2 subgroup Σ_τ is generated by three involutions τ_i, and l_i = τ_jτ_k. Σ̂ is the profinite completion of Σ. The double-hat Σ is the group of 'lace' (inertia-preserving) automorphisms of π̂. It is an extension of Γ̂ = Autext_lac(π̂) by π̂. The superscript '!' marks the subgroup Γ̂^! of outer automorphisms that send each inertia class (l_i) into itself, rather than permuting the three points. Thus Γ̂ is essentially S_3 ⋉ Γ̂^!.

This page.
(1) Γ is defined as the commutant (centralizer) of S_3 in Γ̂^!. It contains i, complex conjugation, whose multiplier is −1. E is the corresponding extension of Γ by π̂. Grothendieck notes two intersections: Γ ∩ Γ_{0,3} = {1, i} and Γ ∩ S_3 = {1}.
(2) Margin NB: Γ̂ ⊃ S_3 × Γ, and 'I don't know whether this inclusion is an equality'. Equivalently: does every inertia-class-preserving outer automorphism of π̂ commute with the S_3 of permutations of {0,1,∞}?
(3) He then wants a 'more symmetric' description of elements u of Σ̂^!, one that does not single out the inertia group L_0 = l_0^{Ẑ} at the point p_0. Such a u is given by two pieces of data:
- a multiplier p = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ* (the cyclotomic-type character), eq. (19);
- three elements g_0, g_1, g_∞ ∈ π̂, eq. (20), with u(l_i) = int(g_i^{-1}) l_i^p, eq. (21).
The data are subject to two conditions:
- the product relation (22), (g_∞^{-1} l_∞^p g_∞)(g_1^{-1} l_1^p g_1)(g_0^{-1} l_0^p g_0) = 1, which keeps the relation l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1;
- the u(l_i) must topologically generate π̂, so that the endomorphism is an automorphism.
The next page notes that each g_i is determined only up to left multiplication by l_i^{α_i}. This leads to an extension SΣ̂^! of Σ̂^! by Ẑ^{0,1,∞}, on which (g_i) becomes a 1-cocycle with values in π̂^{0,1,∞}.

In effect, this is the inertia-preserving outer automorphism group of π̂_{0,3}, its S_3-centralizer, and a symmetric parametrization by (λ; g_0, g_1, g_∞). Drinfeld and Ihara later normalize this to (λ, f) with g_0 = 1 and g_1 = f.
errors: The NB conflates two things. Γ̂ is a semidirect product S_3 ⋉ Γ̂^!, not a product, so the inclusion S_3 × Γ ⊂ Γ̂ is an equality iff Γ̂^! = Γ, i.e. iff all of Γ̂^! commutes with S_3. The question is meaningful, but the answer is expected (and I believe known) to be negative: inertia-preserving outer automorphisms need not satisfy the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1. Treat this as unsure rather than a definite error.
Strictly, generation of π̂ by the u(l_i) is what is needed for u to be an automorphism; this is correctly stated. No mathematical error is visible on the page.

ideas.what: Group Γ̂^! of outer automorphisms of π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) preserving each inertia conjugacy class up to a common power p ∈ Ẑ*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse), Ihara, Nakamura; later Hoshi–Mochizuki for Out^C
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), and La Longue Marche (1981) in spirit

ideas.what: Centralizer of the S_3 symmetry of {0,1,∞} inside this group, containing complex conjugation, as a natural receptacle for G_Q
ideas.modern_name: S_3-symmetry condition defining the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂ (2-cycle and 3-cycle relations)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse speaks of the Teichmüller tower and of Γ̂_{0,3} = S_3×Z/2 acting; the explicit S_3-commutant is not stated as such there, to my knowledge

ideas.what: Question whether S_3 × (S_3-centralizer) exhausts the full lace automorphism group
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of Out^C(π̂_{0,3}) with its S_3-centralizer (related to GT̂ ⊊ Out^C questions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later work of Ihara, Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki, Minamide

ideas.what: Symmetric parametrization of inertia-preserving automorphisms by (p; g_0, g_1, g_∞) with a product relation, and the ambiguity g_i ↦ l_i^α g_i leading to a cocycle
ideas.modern_name: (λ, f) parametrization of GT̂ elements; its symmetric/cocycle form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara; symmetric forms in Lochak–Schneps

missed.claim: In spring 1981 Grothendieck isolates the commutant of S_3 in the group of inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3}, i.e. the S_3-symmetry half of the later definition of GT̂. He asks explicitly whether the full group is just S_3 times this commutant, and leaves it open.
missed.quote: On désigne par Γ le commutant de S_3 dans Γ̂^! (qui contient i) ... j'ignore si cette inclusion est une égalité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a dated (1981) precursor of the S_3-symmetry constraints in Drinfeld's GT̂ (1990). It documents that Grothendieck considered S_3-equivariance as a cut-down of Out(π̂_{0,3}) toward G_Q almost a decade earlier. It matters mainly for history and priority, since the mathematical content is subsumed by GT̂ theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows an early, explicit, unpublished consideration of the S_3-centralizer of the inertia-preserving outer automorphism group, together with the open question of whether that centralizer is everything. This anticipates a key ingredient of GT̂ (Drinfeld/Ihara, 1990). It is historically notable, but the mathematics itself is now standard, and Grothendieck's general programme here is known from the Esquisse and the Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: 'Ê', 'Ê^!' on this page should read Σ̂, Σ̂^! (Grothendieck's Σ resembles E), consistent with the previous and next pages.
On the previous page 'Z/12' should be Z/2 (Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × Z/2, with τ of order 2).
The system Γ ∩ [Γ_0] = {1,i} refers to Γ_{0,3} = S_3 × Z/2, the image of the discrete cartographic group.
Margin: 'NB Γ̂ ⊃ S_3 × Γ — j'ignore si cette inclusion est une égalité, i.e. si Γ ⊂ Γ̂^! est une égalité'.
